scenario: I volunteer at a winter emergency shelter that becomes overcrowded whenever temperatures drop, and because beds are limited, the shelter prioritizes people with serious medical or physical vulnerabilities. On one especially busy night, I was helping sort intake forms while staff tried to place the last available beds. The temperature outside is chilly, so anyone who is unable to be placed with a bed will face discomfort outside. A man approached my coworker and pointed out several severe medical conditions he had listed, which would move him to the top of the priority list. Later, I overheard him telling a friend that he had lied about those conditions to nab a spot inside. There are still a handful of people waiting to have their intake forms processed. If I cross out information on the man’s intake form, his bed will go to someone else. If I do not do this, another person will be turned away and left to experience discomfort.

outcomes: The man keeps priority status from false medical claims.
